target_customer: Startup and small company teams that work in Slack
problem: Team knowledge gets lost in chat and wikis go stale. Niles answers repeated questions in Slack, asks teammates when it does not know, and remembers the answer.

founders.name: Mack Lu
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him with no background. He answered users on Product Hunt.

competitors.name: Obie
competitors.what: Slack chatbot that answers from a team knowledge base

technical_complexity.rationale: Question matching and answer capture inside Slack was feasible with 2017 chatbot tools, but accurate retrieval was hard.

defensibility.rationale: Depended on Slack's platform and was easy for Slack, Guru or wiki vendors to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Guru later announced a Slack integration and investment from the Slack Fund. No acquisition of Niles was found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in March 2017 framed Niles as an alternative to internal wikis that teams rarely keep updated. No spend data was found.

identity.mascot_or_character: Named bot persona, no mascot art found
identity.voice_and_tone: assistant persona that asks teammates for help

branding.brand_signature: A named chat assistant that lives in Slack
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch and Hongkiat in 2017 and had a Product Hunt page.

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly bot name but little brand specific evidence beyond launch coverage.

pivots.to: Real time wiki that turns chats and docs into team knowledge
pivots.why: Product Hunt reply said focus was internal knowledge sharing; YC page uses the wiki wording

outcome_analysis: Niles was a two person Slack bot company from W17 that got launch coverage from TechCrunch in March 2017 but no funding announcement. Its website no longer resolves from this environment and the YC page lists it inactive. The cause is not public, so no failure factor is assigned, though a Slack dependent product with many rivals faced platform and copy risk.
notes: niles.ai did not resolve from this environment (DNS failure) so it is treated as dead or blocked. No funding was found in two searches; Crunchbase has a profile but showed no data. Obie is dated about three months after the batch. The pivot entry is inferred from wording differences and has no date. Product Hunt reply content came from a search summary, not an opened page.
